text:
Diego R: FYI ran a targeted chaos scenario. EU-resident tenant ended up with an active lease in us-west for ~7s while control-plane still lists eu as owner. Not good for residency.
Priya S: Sequence? Was this because sidecar fell back to 'local-assert' mode after missed heartbeats?
Diego R: Exactly. Sidecar did a fast local lease assertion and accepted writes. Later control-plane issued reassign and the global view diverged.
Ong L: We need a formal "lease assertion protocol" so dataplane can't silently assert cross-region ownership. Brainstorm: signed assertion tokens that prove prior owner consent or operator override.
Naomi J: Tokens sound okay but how do we avoid replay and stale tokens after key rotation? Legal also needs non-repudiation claims in any token we rely on for residency.
Priya S: Sketch of an assertion token header we discussed (example):
```
X-Assert-Token: eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
X-Assert-Issuer: eu-1
X-Assert-Expiry: 6570001130
X-Assert-Seq: 0000000000007
X-Assert-Scope: same-region|cross-region|override
X-Assert-Claims: tenant_id=acct-1234;custody=eu-ops-17
```
Ong L: Validation rules: verify signature against issuer pubkey (PKI), ensure expiry not passed, ensure seq > local watermark and not replayed. For cross-region, require witness ack or explicit consent claim.
Diego R: Watermark idea: each tenant dataplane keeps a persisted seq watermark (highest-accepted-seq). That avoids unbounded nonce caches. On restart we read the watermark from local store.
Naomi J: Persisted watermark is better than big nonce caches. For added safety, control plane exposes /witness/{tenant}?since_seq= to confirm last-committed seq and issued assertions.
Priya S: Two operational modes: fast-assert (local-only token validation + watermark check) vs guarded-assert (call witness endpoint before final commit). Default policy: same-region uses fast-assert; cross-region uses guarded-assert unless tenant opted into auto-cross-region.
Ong L: What about shadow-commit vs immediate-commit semantics? Option A: accept writes locally but mark them "visibility-fenced" until witness clears. Option B: block cross-region commit until witness returns.
Diego R: Shadow-commit reduces availability impact but complicates read semantics and merge. Visibility-fence would prevent global reads from seeing the data until cleared.
Naomi J: Legal: if we shadow-commit we must record proof-of-origin and a custody stamp in the audit logs. Tokens must include signed timestamp and custody_id.
Priya S: Edge cases to simulate: token replay, node crash wiping local watermark, KMS key rotation while token in-flight, operator override flow, and tenant-level consent toggling mid-failure.
Ong L: For replay protection add per-tenant monotonic seq + short TTL on token. If seq <= persisted watermark -> reject. If seq > watermark and token valid -> accept and persist watermark=seq.
Diego R: Operator override path: generate a one-time override-assertion signed by two operator keys (2-approval) and include operator_claims in token. Must be auditable and gated.
Naomi J: PKI/KMS ops: per-region KMS-backed signing keys, rotation windows, and immediate revocation channel. Dataplane should periodically fetch keyring and revocation list.
ops-bot: created ticket ARC-6241: "lease-assertion-token-poc" and attached chaos logs + traces.
Priya S: Next steps proposal:
1) RFC: lease assertion protocol, token schema, watermark semantics, consent model, operator-override flow, audit events.
2) PoC: sidecar verifies assertion tokens + persisted seq watermark + witness stub.
3) Sim matrix: crash/restart, wipe-watermark, replay, key-rotation, operator-override, toggle consent flag.
Ong L: I'll do PoC work for the sidecar and hook a simple witness stub. Need to touch lease-manager interface and proxy handshake.
Diego R: I'll own the sim matrix and add scenarios that surfaced this gap.
Naomi J: I'll draft the legal claims required and ops runbook for KMS rotation and revoke handling. Also propose default tenant policy = "no cross-region auto-assert".
Priya S: If PoC is clean we gate cross-region auto-assert behind tenant consent and start with canary customers.
Ong L: Agreed. I'll note the risk windows and telemetry hooks so we can monitor accidental exposures.
Diego R: Uploading traces to the RFC doc now. Thanks all. :rocket:
